title: Magazine Commissioning And Issue Planning Desk

stages.name: interpretPitches
stages.algorithm: Read pitches against the issue brief to identify the actual angle, reporting plan, and audience value. Distinguish an interesting topic from a viable story, preserve uncertainty about access or evidence, and identify overlap with already commissioned work.
stages.gate: Pitch evaluation is grounded in the supplied editorial goals and feasible reporting.

stages.name: mapCoverage
stages.algorithm: Build a map of themes, formats, perspectives, and reader needs across proposed pieces. Identify genuine gaps and redundancy without forcing artificial balance between unsupported claims, and preserve coherent variety rather than filling slots mechanically.
stages.gate: Coverage choices follow the issue brief and available evidence.

stages.name: commissionPieces
stages.algorithm: Draft precise commissions specifying angle, scope, length, reporting obligations, rights, and deadlines. Identify dependencies such as interviews or photography, obtain contributor acceptance, and avoid assuming a pitch implies agreement to changed terms.
stages.gate: Contributor accepts the exact scope and commercial conditions before work is committed.

stages.name: manageEditorialWork
stages.algorithm: Compare drafts with commissions and source evidence, formulate specific revisions, and coordinate editing, fact-checking, art, and legal or rights review where needed. Preserve author voice while distinguishing stylistic preference from factual or structural defects.
stages.gate: Required reporting and evidence obligations are fulfilled, not merely polished prose.

stages.name: qualifyIssue
stages.algorithm: Reconcile final pieces, captions, headlines, credits, layout, and publication timing as one issue. Check that promotional language does not overstate article claims, preserve contingency plans for late withdrawals, and freeze the approved edition.
stages.gate: Complete issue meets scope, rights, factual, and production gates.

operational_details: A contributor loses access to a key source: revise the commission rather than pretending the reporting plan still holds.
Two pieces cover the same angle: negotiate differentiation before drafting duplicates.
A headline overstates the article: include it in factual review.
A late withdrawal leaves a section gap: use a prequalified contingency piece.
A photo credit changes: update print, web, and promotional assets consistently.

scenario.representative_episode: An issue has several similar pitches, a missing practical perspective, and a commissioned feature whose central interview becomes unavailable.
scenario.independent_truth: Generated editorial briefs, pitch evidence plans, exact schedules and dependencies, rights conditions, and editorial quality review.
